newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Brash sees declining rate trend-letter to ed..
newsitem.headline: NZ's Brash sees declining rate trend-letter to ed..

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said on Friday that he has no doubt interest rates will continue on a declining trend as New Zealand builds up a record for low inflation.

In a letter to the editor of The Independent business weekly newspaper Brash defended the need for low inflation and said the only way to reduce interest rates in a sustainable way was to convince borrowers and savers alike that inflation would stay low indefinitely.
"It is no accident that as New Zealand's inflation rate has declined over the last decade, our interest rates have also declined substantially," Brash said.

"I have no doubt that, as we continue to build a record for predictably low inflation, interest rates will continue a declining trend, though with inevitable fluctuations around that trend as the supply of, and demand for, borrowed money ebbs and flows," he said.
Brash was replying to a report in the newspaper which had suggested that the central bank was obsessed with low inflation.
He said there was a consensus among economists that low inflation enabled economies to work effectively.
He said it was correct to say that the gains of price stability to exporters were offset by rises in the currency.
But he said exporters received "very important" indirect benefits from price stability. In particularly it focused exporters on improving their businesses.
